quote: It is not out of hatred that the Lord chides human beings, for he suffered for us when he could have destroyed us because of our faults. For he is a good Teacher who has the consummate ability to censure with words of rebuke. His words of reproach are like a whip that scourges the sluggish mind of people. And then, once he scourges them, he can move on to exhorting them. For those who are not motivated by praise are spurred on by censure. And those whom censure cannot rouse to salvation, as if they were dead, are by denunciation roused to the truth. "For the whip and correction are suited in every circumstance to wisdom."

Let us attempt to do also that which wisdom admonishes, saying: "drink waters from your own springs, and from your own wells, and let your own fountain be your own." Attempt therefore, you also, O hearer, to have your own well and your own fountain; that you too, when you have taken hold of the book of the scriptures, may begin even from your own understanding to bring forth some meaning, and according to those things which you have learned in the church, attempt you also to drink from the fountain of your own natural ability. There is within you the nature of "living water," there are perennial veins and irrigating streams of rational understanding, if only they be not filled up with earth and rubble. But be diligent to dig your earth and to purge the filth, that is, to remove the sloth of your natural ability and to shake off the torpor of your heart. For hear what the Scripture says:…

But since the same blessed Apostle bids us become imitators of this grace, that is, of the prophetic gift, as being in some part and within our power, saying: "but be zealous for the better gifts, and rather that you may prophesy", let us too attempt to take up a zeal for good things and to exert whatever is in us, but to await from the Lord the fullness of the gift. For with regard to the one it is said by the Lord through the prophet: "open thy mouth, and I will fill it", but with regard to the other another Scripture says: "prick the eye, and it brings forth a tear; prick the heart, and it brings forth understanding".
